title: feat(spec): sharing / approval / report enforcement takes the full ExecutionContext (#6523)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6523

The #6206 ruling default — converge on the full envelope, keep no per-site subset
contracts — applied to its fourth and widest twin. Contract face only: the
`plugin-sharing` / `plugin-approvals` / `plugin-reports` implementation bodies are
untouched and no runtime behaviour changes.

## What changed

`packages/spec/src/contracts/` — **36 signatures across three files** now declare their
context parameter as the complete `ExecutionContext` instead of the six-field
`SharingExecutionContext`:

| contract file | interfaces | signatures |
|:---|:---|---:|
| `sharing-service.ts` | `ISharingService`, `ISharingRuleService` | 15 |
| `approval-service.ts` | `IApprovalService` | 12 |
| `report-service.ts` | `IReportService` | 9 |

Every one of them ADJUDICATES access — the read-filter contribution, both write gates and
their #6428 tri-state forms, share management, rule definition and evaluation, approval
decisions / recalls / reassignments, report runs and schedules — so each needs the whole
`resolveAuthzContext` result: `accessible_org_ids` (the `group`-posture Layer 0 wall,
ADR-0105 D2), `org_user_ids`, `systemPermissions`, `posture` (ADR-0095 D2 — resolved once,
carried, never re-derived at the enforcement site) and `tabPermissions`.

Shape follows the #6430 / PR #6511 precedent exactly, with no third variant invented:
reference the existing `ExecutionContext` (`kernel/execution-context.zod.js`, the
`z.input` caller-side envelope) at the enforcement signatures, and keep the narrow type
EXPORTED and UNCHANGED IN SHAPE with TSDoc stating the boundary. Widening
`SharingExecutionContext` field-by-field was the option deliberately not taken — it
rebuilds the per-site subset the ruling removed, one field at a time, and PR #6511 pinned
that same refusal for its own twin.

## The MIRROR direction — the part a reviewer does not expect

At the share-link site the caller trimmed the VALUE before enforcement saw it. Here
nothing was trimmed. `plugin-sharing`'s engine middleware passes its whole execution
context down —

```ts
// packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts:860
let filter = await service.buildReadFilter(ctx.object, exec ?? {});
```

— so the values always arrived complete. It was the declared TYPE that was narrow, so the
receiving implementation could not READ what it had been handed without casting out of
its own contract. The measured specimen, live on `origin/main` at `08863dd18`, inside
`plugin-approvals`' privileged-override gate:

```ts
// packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts:661 — isOverrideActor()
const posture = (context as any).posture;
```

— whose own doc comment says it reads "the derived `posture`, ADR-0095" off the resolved
exec context. That is #6206's "declared narrow, consumed narrow" seen from the other end,
and it is why this card earns its diff: an `as any` on an enforcement input switches off
checking for the whole expression, so the next field read through it is unverified too,
and it makes the honest reading of the gate indistinguishable from a typo.

## Premise verification (the line numbers moved; the premise held)

The issue was written against `ecff95108`; base here is `08863dd18`. Re-verified on the
current base:

- `SharingExecutionContext` still declares exactly six fields, still at
  `sharing-service.ts:117`, still missing the four the ruling named.
- Three contracts still share it — measured 15 / 12 / 9 = 36 parameter positions (the
  issue estimated 11 approval / 10 report from an older tree).
- The call site cited as `sharing-plugin.ts:796` is now `:860`, otherwise unchanged.
- The shape consequence the issue predicted **without testing** is not only real but
  already paid — the `(context as any).posture` above is an implementor who hit exactly
  this wall.

## Acceptance surface: zero change

TypeScript interfaces, not Zod schemas. Nothing authorable moves, no `safeParse` verdict
changes, and `SharingExecutionContext` is still an exported interface, so
`api-surface/contracts.json` is byte-identical:

```
@objectstack/spec public API surface + factory signatures unchanged ✓
✓ All 10 generated artifacts are up to date.
```

## Reverse verification — direction predicted BEFORE the run, and one honest correction

Predicted: revert the widening and the shape-witness pin goes RED, because the
implementation can no longer read the envelope fields. Measured with the three contract
files reverted to `origin/main` and the pin test left in place
(`tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`) — 22 errors on the pin file, zero before:

```
sharing-service.test.ts(586,37): error TS2339: Property 'accessible_org_ids' does not exist on type 'SharingExecutionContext'.
sharing-service.test.ts(588,26): error TS2339: Property 'posture' does not exist on type 'SharingExecutionContext'.
sharing-service.test.ts(589,31): error TS2339: Property 'org_user_ids' does not exist on type 'SharingExecutionContext'.
sharing-service.test.ts(590,33): error TS2551: Property 'tabPermissions' does not exist on type 'SharingExecutionContext'. Did you mean 'permissions'?
      9 error TS2322     (the identity-pin tuple)
      3 error TS2339     (the envelope reads)
      9 error TS2344     (Assert/Refute on the six identity pins + three refutations)
      1 error TS2551     (tabPermissions — tsc suggests `permissions`)
```

Two things worth stating plainly rather than dressing to match the template:

1. **The TS2551 is the whole card in one line.** tsc's "Did you mean `permissions`?" is
   the exact near-miss the narrow type invited — `permissions` (permission-set names) and
   `tabPermissions` (tab visibility) are different authorities, and the narrow type left
   only the wrong one reachable.
2. **There is NO TS2353 here, and there should not be.** PR #6511's before-red was
   excess-property at a call site stating a trimmed envelope; this pin passes the envelope
   as an annotated variable, exactly as the engine middleware does, because in this
   direction the value was always whole and always assignable — only the READ was blocked.
   Manufacturing an inline literal to harvest a second error class would have made the
   pin look like #6511's and misdescribe the defect.

## Cross-package type change: does the widened type still reject an unknown key (#6218)

Yes — `ExecutionContext` is a closed set, not a bag. Feeding a key it does not declare:

```
error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties,
  and 'not_a_context_key' does not exist in type
  '{ userId?: string | undefined; actor?: string | undefined; ... 23 more ...; traceId?: string | undefined; }'.
```

## Consumption-radius typecheck — the verification body of this card

Direction stated explicitly (#6218): the **DEPENDENTS** direction,
`pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '...@objectstack/spec' typecheck` (leading dots
= everything that consumes the changed contracts; `spec` has no workspace dependencies,
so the other direction is empty). Result: **exit 0**, every consumer package green,
`plugin-approvals` / `plugin-sharing` / `plugin-reports` included.

That green IS the substantive claim of this PR: a TS interface parameter widened to a type
that is mutually assignable with the old one breaks neither implementors (all six fields
exist in `ExecutionContext` with compatible types, nothing there is required, and method
parameters are bivariant besides) nor callers.

⚠️ Stated the way PR #6511 had to state its own: **no compiler was waiting to push the
consumer half.** Nothing goes red from this change, so the `as any` above does not
disappear on its own — it has to be removed deliberately. Filed, not assumed (below).

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.test.ts` gains one describe block, three
cases:

1. **Type identity across all three contracts** — the context parameter of a
   representative adjudicating method on each interface IS `ExecutionContext`, asserted by
   identity so re-narrowing to anything goes red, plus refutations that it is no longer
   the six-field twin.
2. **The shape witness** — an implementation typed BY THE CONTRACT
   (`ISharingService['buildReadFilter']`, not by a local annotation) reads
   `accessible_org_ids` / `posture` / `org_user_ids` / `tabPermissions` with **no
   `as any`**, fed by a call site spelled the way the engine middleware spells it.
   Anti-vacuity: the fake records what it received and the case asserts the values really
   travelled.
3. **The narrow twin is unchanged in shape** — its key set is pinned, so the convergence
   cannot be undone by widening it back one field at a time.

Deliberately NOT pinned, for the reason PR #6511 recorded for its own twin: there is no
`@ts-expect-error` asserting that a `SharingExecutionContext` is REJECTED where an
`ExecutionContext` is expected, because it is not — structural subtyping accepts it, so
such a directive would be unsatisfied and fail the build. A pin shaped like compiler
enforcement where only a declaration exists reads as verified and is worse than saying so.

## Test + gate output

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec tsc --noEmit          exit 0
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck                  exit 0
  check:test-typecheck: OK — 58 file(s) / 266 error(s) held in test-typecheck-debt.json (unchanged)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test                       exit 0
  Test Files  351 passed (351)
  Tests       9134 passed (9134)
pnpm --filter '...@objectstack/spec' typecheck             exit 0   (dependents direction)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated            ✓ All 10 generated artifacts are up to date.
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:api-surface      public API surface + factory signatures unchanged ✓
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:exported-any     ✓ 2420 types + 1517 schemas across 16 entry points
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:dual-source-exports  ✓ 0 new dual-source exports
pnpm check:type-check-debt                                 OK — 33 entries re-measured, none above its recorded number
node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs                           OK (scanned 6498 tracked text files)
node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main   ✓ no declared-breaking changeset
```

The 60 gate commands enumerated one by one out of `.github/workflows/lint.yml` all run
inside CI's **ESLint** job (together with `pnpm lint` itself), which is the authoritative
run for them and is **green on this head** — so the local queue entry that would have
re-run the same 60 commands was cancelled while still waiting on the shared verification
lock rather than duplicating a result CI had already produced. CI convergence on
`d4ced55c2`, read as job conclusions and not as the aggregate status:

| job | conclusion |
|:---|:---|
| **ESLint** (carries `pnpm lint` + all 60 family gates) | success |
| **TypeScript Type Check** (workspace typecheck, `check:type-check-debt`, api-surface, exported-any, dual-source) | success |
| Build Core / Test Core (1-3/3) | success |
| Check Changeset / Spec property liveness / ADR maintainer approval | success |
| Dogfood Regression Gate (1-3/3) / Dogfood Verify CLI / Temporal Conformance | success |

26 check runs, 24 success, 2 path-skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate), zero failures.

## One number observed but deliberately NOT claimed

`pnpm check:type-check-debt` reports `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` TEST_DEBT at 348
measured against 547 recorded (`-199`). The gate is green either way (below the ceiling is
informational), but I could not cheaply attribute that drop, and the ledger's own note
says the 547 was last re-measured at `5ab08428` — many merges ago. It would have been
convenient to present it as this change unblocking 199 hidden type errors; it is not
measured, so it is not claimed. The surplus itself is already tracked by #6376, which the
gate output names.

## Out of scope, filed not fixed

**Filed as #7070** — the consumer half: the three implementations still annotate their own
parameters with `SharingExecutionContext` (27 + 21 + 14 refs), which is why
`(context as any).posture` is still needed to read a field the contract now declares.
Separated exactly as #6430's contract half and its plugin half were, and labelled
`finding` rather than queued: there is no user-visible defect, the values are complete at
runtime and always were. #6216 (the three assembly SITES of `ExecutionContext`)
is a different card and was not touched.
